items.question: What other exercises can help John with his basketball performance?
items.answer:
Since you’re already lifting and doing yoga, these additions will round out your game as a shooting guard and support your goals (better shooting %, speed, and durability):

- Plyometrics (1–2x/week): box jumps, depth jumps, lateral bounds, pogo jumps to boost first‑step and vertical.
- Agility/change‑of‑direction: 5‑10‑5 shuttle, T‑drill, cone zigzags with defensive slides, closeout-and‑recover to sharpen lateral quickness.
- Speed/acceleration: resisted sled sprints, 10–20 m starts, flying 30s for top‑end speed and repeat sprint ability.
- Core/anti‑rotation: Pallof presses, dead bugs, cable chops, farmer’s carries to stabilize on drives and contests.
- Single‑leg strength: Bulgarian split squats, step‑ups, single‑leg RDLs for balance, power, and injury resistance.
- Posterior chain/power: trap‑bar deadlifts, hip thrusts, kettlebell swings; add med‑ball chest/overhead/rotational throws for explosive force.
- Ankle/foot resilience (given your past ankle rehab): straight/bent‑knee calf raises, tibialis raises, ankle mobility/dorsiflexion drills, single‑leg balance with reach, hop matrix (forward/lateral/diagonal).
- Shoulder/scap prehab for shooting volume: band external rotations, face pulls, Y‑T‑W raises, serratus wall slides to keep the shot smooth and shoulders healthy.
- Mobility focus: hip flexor/hamstring work, ankle dorsiflexion, and thoracic spine openers to maintain fluid movement and shooting mechanics.
- Conditioning (court‑specific): intervals like suicides, “17s,” 3‑2‑1 drills; low‑impact options (bike/rower intervals) on lighter days.
- Reaction/decision speed: tennis‑ball drops, partner cue drills, light‑reaction drills (e.g., BlazePod) to improve reads and closeouts.
- Shooting under fatigue (ties to your % goal): catch‑and‑shoot off relocations/pindowns, one‑dribble pull‑ups, spot‑to‑spot sprints with FT pressure (e.g., 5 makes, sprint, 2 FTs).
- Ball‑handling/footwork: two‑ball dribbles, change‑of‑pace combos around cones, jab‑series, stop‑on‑a‑dime into step‑backs to create space cleanly.

Simple structure: 1–2 plyo/agility days, 2 short conditioning blocks, daily 10–15 min ankle/shoulder prehab, and finish skill sessions with game‑speed shooting. This complements your strength work and yoga and should translate directly to on‑court performance.
